Secondary 9th Chords · Level 1.heading: Hear the chord. Choose its ninth-chord type.
Secondary 9th Chords · Level 1.intro: You will hear a ninth chord with a different combination of chord notes. Choose the chord type that matches the sound.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play and listen to the notes together. Notice the overall sound, rather than trying to name every note. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Choose the chord name that matches what you hear. The answer buttons show the six chord types used in this lesson.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

Secondary 9th Chords · Level 1.about: These ninth chords use different combinations of chord notes. For example, Minor-Major 9th combines a minor three-note chord with a major seventh and a ninth. In F, those notes are F, A♭, C, E and G. In the answer names, ♭5 means the fifth is lowered by one keyboard step, and ♯5 means it is raised by one keyboard step, counting both white and black keys. This lesson uses chords built on F. The root, the note the chord is named after, stays at the bottom. Choose only the chord type; there is no separate inversion answer.
Secondary 9th Chords · Level 1.layoutCaption: F minor-major ninth: F, A♭ and C, with E and G added above them.
Secondary 9th Chords · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example is F minor-major ninth. Choose Minor-Major 9th. During the quiz, choose the type of chord you hear, even when the notes are arranged differently.
